title: Define deterministic resource-budget and quota contracts
businessObjective: Prevent AI/staff workloads from exhausting capacity or affecting booking operations.
technicalObjective: Define finite quota budget, threshold, state, metering-freshness, and fail-closed decision contracts without connecting to a provider meter.
assumptions: Budgets are deterministic policy inputs, not live provider configuration.
acceptanceCriteria: Contract covers worker requests/CPU, queue operations, workflow steps, persistence size/growth/egress, runner minutes, AI invocations/tokens, and notification volume.
It defines 50%, 75%, and 90% warning thresholds and a pre-hard-limit fail-closed pause/requeue/block decision.

Missing, unavailable, stale, inconsistent, uncertain, or unknown metrics, budgets, limits, metering timestamps, or configuration fail closed with deterministic reasons and cannot affect booking capacity.
Workload rules require batching, dedupe, idempotency, backpressure, rate/concurrency/retry bounds, DLQ, priority queues, and scheduled summaries.
Tests reject every metering-uncertainty state, unbounded or per-event AI, and booking-shared quota cases.
requiredChecks: exact validator admission before independent verification
solEscalationTriggers: Any resource control changes booking capacity, provider quotas, live scheduling, or production behavior.
rollbackExpectations: Revert static contracts only and preserve evidence.
